paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: in Proverbs 13, every road has a direction, and Solomon wants you to see where each one ends. Listening to correction leads to honor, and ignoring it leads to "Poverty and shame" (Proverbs 13:18). A guarded mouth protects a life, and a lazy streak craves and gets nothing (Proverbs 13:3-4). Solomon isn't trying to scare you. He's handing you a map before you start the trip.

Now look at the line that sits right in the middle of all those matchups: "He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed" (Proverbs 13:20). Wisdom is not just something you collect, friend. It rubs off on you, like flour on my apron after one batch. So the question is not only what you know. It's WHO you're walking with, and who is listening to you.

Here's the part that gets me. The teaching of the wise is "a fountain of life" (Proverbs 13:14), and Solomon says a fulfilled desire is "a tree of life" (Proverbs 13:12). He doesn't call correction a punishment. He calls it a gift that turns you from the snares of death. So this week, baker, pick one voice you will actually listen to, and keep your ears open for it.
